marking_schemes.question_text:
Which gas decolourises potassium permanganate (KMnO4) solution?
(a) Sulphur dioxide
(b) Ammonia
(c) Hydrogen chloride
(d) Carbon dioxide
key_points: Sulphur dioxide decolourises KMnO4 due to its reducing properties
common_errors: Confusion between sulphur dioxide and carbon dioxide
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. A few confused SO2 with CO2.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Which formula represents a saturated hydrocarbon?
(a) C4H8
(b) C5H12
(c) C4H6
(d) C5H10
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (b) C5H12 / pentane / correct structural formula as well as condensed form
key_points: Saturated hydrocarbons follow CnH2n+2 formula
C5H12 is pentane, an alkane
common_errors: Confusion between C5H12 and C5H10; selecting C5H10 as saturated
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates correctly identified C5H12. Some confused it with C5H10.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The metal whose oxide can be reduced by common reducing agents:
(a) Copper
(b) Sodium
(c) Aluminium
(d) Potassium
key_points: Copper is a less reactive metal; its oxide can be reduced by common reducing agents like H2, C, CO
common_errors: Choosing sodium or aluminium
Some candidates selected multiple answers
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates correctly identified copper. Some struggled with the concept of metal reactivity and reducing agents.

marking_schemes.question_text:
An organic compound has a vapour density of 22. The molecular formula of the organic compound is: [Atomic weight: C = 12, H = 1]
(a) CH4
(b) C2H4
(c) C2H6
(d) C3H8
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (d) C3H8 / propane / correct structural formula as well as condensed form
key_points: Molecular mass = 2 x vapour density = 2 x 22 = 44
C3H8 has molecular mass = 36+8 = 44
common_errors: Choosing C2H6 due to incorrect formula application
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most answered correctly as C3H8. A few chose C2H6 due to confusion with formula.

marking_schemes.question_text:
In the reaction given below sulphuric acid acts as a/an:
S + 2H2SO4 → 3SO2 + 2H2O
(a) Non-volatile acid
(b) Dibasic acid
(c) Oxidising agent
(d) Reducing agent
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) Oxidising agent / Oxidizing / Oxidizing property / Oxidised / Oxidation / Ox
key_points: Sulphur is oxidised from 0 to +4 in SO2; H2SO4 acts as oxidising agent
common_errors: Confusion between oxidising agent and reducing agent
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. Some struggled with identifying oxidising vs reducing agent.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Assertion (A): The tendency of losing electrons increases down the Group.
Reason (R): The most reactive metal is placed at the top of Group 1.
(a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(c) (A) is true but (R) is false.
(d) (A) is false but (R) is true.
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
key_points: Tendency to lose electrons increases down the group — TRUE
Most reactive metal is at BOTTOM of Group 1, not top — R is FALSE
common_errors: Incorrectly choosing option (a) or (b) due to difficulty correlating A and R
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority correctly identified option (c). Some found it challenging to correlate A and R statements.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text:
The ore that can be concentrated by using magnetic separation:
(a) Corundum
(b) Haematite
(c) Calamine
(d) Bauxite
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (b) Haematite / Fe2O3 / Ferric oxide / Iron(III) oxide
key_points: Haematite (Fe2O3) is a magnetic iron ore that can be concentrated by magnetic separation
common_errors: Choosing bauxite instead of haematite
Some chose corundum or calamine
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. Some confused haematite with bauxite.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The diagram shows the bonding in the covalent molecule AB2. Which option represents the correct electronic configuration of atoms A and B before combining together to form the above molecule?
(a) A: 2,4 | B: 2,8,6
(b) A: 2,4 | B: 2,8,7
(c) A: 2,8 | B: 2,8,8
(d) A: 2,6 | B: 2,8,7
key_points: A has 2,6 (6 valence electrons, needs 2 to complete octet, forms 2 bonds)
B has 2,8,7 (7 valence electrons, needs 1 to complete octet, forms 1 bond)
AB2 means A forms 2 bonds, consistent with A needing 2 electrons
common_errors: Considering electronic configuration after combination instead of before
Mistakenly choosing option (c)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates did not comprehend 'before combining together'. Some mistakenly chose option (c).

marking_schemes.question_text:
Which of the following options has all the compounds which are members of the same homologous series?
(a) CH4, C2H6, C3H8
(b) CH4, C2H6, C3H6
(c) C3H4, C3H6, C3H8
(d) C2H4, C3H6, C4H10
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (a) CH4, C2H6, C3H8 / methane, ethane, propane
key_points: All three follow alkane general formula CnH2n+2
Each member differs by CH2
marking_schemes.model_answer: (a) CH4, C2H6, C3H8 (methane, ethane, propane — all alkanes)
common_errors: Confusion between option (a) and (b)
Failing to identify general formulas for alkanes, alkenes, alkynes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Answered well by many but quite a few confused option (a) and (b). Many failed to identify general formulas for each series.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Assertion (A): In the Contact Process SO3 gas is not directly dissolved in water to obtain sulphuric acid.
Reason (R): Dense fog or misty droplets of sulphuric acid are formed which is difficult to condense.
(a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(c) (A) is true but (R) is false.
(d) (A) is false but (R) is true.
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
marking_schemes.correct_answer: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
key_points: SO3 is dissolved in oleum (H2S2O7) not water to avoid acid mist formation
marking_schemes.model_answer: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
common_errors: Mistakenly thinking SO3 can be directly dissolved in water, choosing option (d)
Misunderstanding 'dense fog' formed
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered correctly. Some mistakenly considered SO3 can be dissolved in water.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Given below are four ions: Cl–, Li+, Al3+, K+
Identify the pair of ions which have the same electronic configuration.
[Atomic number: Cl = 17, Li = 3, Al = 13, K = 19]
(a) Cl– & Li+
(b) Al3+ & K+
(c) Cl– & K+
(d) Li+ & K+
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) Cl– & K+ / Chloride ion & Potassium ion / Chloride & Potassium ion
key_points: Cl– has 18 electrons: 2,8,8
K+ has 18 electrons: 2,8,8
Both have same electronic configuration as Argon
common_errors: Confusion between Li and K
Errors in number of electrons gained/lost
Confusion between options (c) and (d)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified option (c). Common errors included confusion about electrons gained/lost when forming ions.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text:
Which pair of reactants can be best used to produce lead (II) sulphate?
(a) Sulphuric acid + Lead
(b) Sulphuric acid + Lead hydroxide
(c) Sodium sulphate + Lead nitrate
(d) Potassium sulphate + Lead oxide
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) Sodium sulphate + Lead nitrate / Na2SO4 and Pb(NO3)2
key_points: Lead sulphate is insoluble; best prepared by double displacement/precipitation
Na2SO4 + Pb(NO3)2 → PbSO4↓ + 2NaNO3
common_errors: Many did not understand concept of double displacement reaction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates failed. Many did not understand double displacement reaction. Only a few identified correct answer.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Aqueous copper (II) sulphate is electrolysed using copper electrodes. Which statement about the electrolysis is NOT correct?
(a) An oxidation reaction occurs at the positive electrode.
(b) The current is carried through the electrolyte by ions.
(c) The positive electrode loses mass.
(d) The number of copper (II) ions in the electrolyte decreases.
options: (a) An oxidation reaction occurs at the positive electrode.
(b) The current is carried through the electrolyte by ions.
(d) The number of copper (II) ions in the electrolyte decreases.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: (d) The number of copper (II) ions in the electrolyte decreases.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (d) The number of copper (II) ions in the electrolyte decreases.
key_points: With active copper electrodes, anode dissolves and cathode gains copper
Concentration of Cu2+ ions remains unchanged — so (d) is NOT correct
marking_schemes.model_answer: (d) The number of copper (II) ions in the electrolyte decreases.
common_errors: Overlooking the word 'not' in the question
Forgetting that Cu2+ concentration remains unchanged with copper electrodes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most chose correctly. However many overlooked 'not' in question. A significant number forgot that Cu2+ concentration remains unchanged with copper electrodes.

marking_schemes.question_text:
X, Y & Z are three metallic atoms in successive order belonging to the same group such that atomic radii of 'X' is the smallest. Which of the three atoms is the best reducing agent?
(a) X
(b) Y
(c) Z
(d) All three have the same reducing power.
options: (d) All three have the same reducing power.
key_points: Down the group, atomic radius increases, ionisation energy decreases
Larger atoms lose electrons more easily — better reducing agents
Z has the largest atomic radius, so it is the best reducing agent
common_errors: Relating small size with best reducing agent and selecting X
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered correctly as Z. Some related small size with best reducing agent and selected X incorrectly.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text:
40 cm3 of methane (CH4) is reacted with 60 cm3 of oxygen.
CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O
All volumes are measured at room temperature. What is the total volume of the gases remaining at the end of the reaction?
(a) 60 cm3
(b) 40 cm3
(c) 45 cm3
(d) 50 cm3
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (b) 40 cm3 / 40 / 10 cc CH4 and 30 cc CO2
key_points: 40 cm3 CH4 needs 80 cm3 O2 but only 60 cm3 O2 available — O2 is limiting
O2 reacts with 30 cm3 CH4 (60/2=30 cm3 CH4 reacts)
CH4 remaining = 40-30 = 10 cm3
CO2 produced = 30 cm3
H2O is liquid at room temperature — not counted
Total gas = 10 cm3 CH4 + 30 cm3 CO2 = 40 cm3
marking_schemes.model_answer: (b) 40 cm3 (10 cm3 CH4 unreacted + 30 cm3 CO2 produced)
common_errors: Marking 60 cm3 due to confusion
Calculating volume of gases formed but not total remaining
Not accounting for H2O being liquid at room temperature
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority selected correct answer 40 cm3. Many marked 60 cm3 due to confusion. Some calculated volume of gases formed, not total volume remaining.

marking_schemes.question_text: A student was instructed by the teacher to prepare and collect ammonia gas in the laboratory by using aluminium nitride. The student set up the apparatus with aluminium nitride in a flask and a thistle funnel. Name the substance X added through the thistle funnel by the student.
key_points: Warm/hot water reacts with aluminium nitride to produce ammonia
common_errors: Writing simply 'water' without specifying warm/hot
Writing concentrated sulphuric acid
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many correctly identified warm water. Several simply wrote water. A significant number wrote concentrated sulphuric acid.

marking_schemes.question_text: A student was instructed by the teacher to prepare and collect ammonia gas in the laboratory by using aluminium nitride. Write a balanced equation for the reaction occurring between Aluminium nitride and substance X (warm water).
key_points: Correct reactants: AlN and H2O
Correct products: Al(OH)3 and NH3
Equation must be balanced
common_errors: Writing sulphuric acid in reactant instead of water
Writing aluminium oxide instead of aluminium hydroxide as product
Unbalanced equation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many unable to write correct balanced equation. Several confused reactants and products.

marking_schemes.question_text: A student was instructed by the teacher to prepare and collect ammonia gas in the laboratory by using aluminium nitride. The apparatus included a drying agent Y. Identify the substance Y.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: CaO / Calcium oxide / quick lime / lime
marking_schemes.scheme_text: CaO / Calcium oxide / quick lime / lime
key_points: Calcium oxide is used to dry ammonia gas
CaO is alkaline, so it does not react with ammonia
common_errors: Writing concentrated sulphuric acid as drying agent
Writing calcium hydroxide
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified Y as calcium oxide. A few wrote concentrated sulphuric acid or calcium hydroxide.

marking_schemes.question_text: A student was instructed by the teacher to prepare and collect ammonia gas in the laboratory by using aluminium nitride. State the function of Y (CaO/calcium oxide).
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Drying agent / to absorb moisture / to remove water / to dry gas
marking_schemes.scheme_text: drying agent / to absorb moisture / to remove water / to dry gas
key_points: CaO acts as a drying agent to remove moisture from ammonia gas
marking_schemes.model_answer: Y (CaO) acts as a drying agent — it absorbs moisture/water from the ammonia gas.
common_errors: Confusing drying agent with dehydrating agent
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates confused drying agent with dehydrating agent and answered incorrectly.

marking_schemes.question_text: A student was instructed by the teacher to prepare and collect ammonia gas in the laboratory by using aluminium nitride. Why could the student NOT collect ammonia gas at the end of the experiment? (The collection vessel contained water.)
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Ammonia gas is soluble in water / dissolves in water / highly soluble in water / miscible in water / forms ammonium hydroxide / is collected by downward displacement of air / by upward delivery of gas
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Ammonia gas is soluble in water / dissolves in water / highly soluble in water / miscible in water / forms ammonium hydroxide / is collected by downward displacement of air / by upward delivery of gas
key_points: Ammonia is highly soluble in water and cannot be collected over water
marking_schemes.model_answer: Ammonia gas is highly soluble in water and dissolves in it to form ammonium hydroxide, so it cannot be collected over water.
common_errors: Unable to explain why ammonia is collected by downward displacement of air
Not aware of high solubility of ammonia in water
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered correctly. Some could not explain the downward displacement method. A few wrote how gas is collected without reading the question.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the term for the following: Undistilled alcohol containing a large amount of methanol.
key_points: Spurious alcohol or illicit alcohol contains methanol which is toxic
common_errors: Writing denatured alcohol or methylated spirit instead
Writing incomplete terms like 'illicit' or 'methylated'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many could not recall 'spurious alcohol' and confused it with denatured alcohol or methylated spirit.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the term for the following: A salt formed by the partial replacement of the hydroxyl group of a di-acidic or a tri-acidic base by an acid radical.
key_points: Basic salt retains some OH groups from the base
common_errors: Confusing with alkaline salt or acidic salt
Copying 'di acidic base' from question
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Only a few with clear understanding answered correctly. Many confused it with alkaline or acidic salt.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the term for the following: Organic compounds having the same molecular formula but different structural formula.
key_points: Isomers have same molecular formula but different structural arrangement
common_errors: Writing 'isomerism' instead of 'isomers'
Writing isotope or homologous series
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most answered correctly. Some confused 'isomer' with 'isomerism'. A few wrote 'isotope'.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the term for the following: The tendency of an atom to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself when combined in a compound.
key_points: Electronegativity is the ability of an atom to attract shared electron pairs
common_errors: Writing electron affinity or ionisation potential
Writing electron negativity or EN
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority wrote correct term. Some wrote electron affinity or ionisation potential incorrectly.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the term for the following: The type of covalent bond in which electrons are shared unequally between the combining atoms.
key_points: In a polar covalent bond, electrons are shared unequally due to electronegativity difference
common_errors: Confusing with non-polar covalent bond or coordinate covalent bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified polar covalent bond. Some confused with non-polar or coordinate covalent bond.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct word from the brackets: ____________ solution forms a coloured precipitate with ammonium hydroxide which is soluble in excess of ammonium hydroxide. [Ferrous chloride / Copper nitrate]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Copper nitrate / Copper (II) nitrate / Cu(NO3)2 / Cupric nitrate
key_points: Copper nitrate forms blue precipitate of Cu(OH)2 with NH4OH which dissolves in excess to give deep blue tetraamminecopper(II) complex
common_errors: Choosing ferrous chloride instead of copper nitrate
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few mistakenly chose ferrous chloride due to confusion about precipitate formation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct word from the brackets: Zinc blende is converted to zinc oxide by __________. [Calcination / Roasting]
key_points: Zinc blende (ZnS) is converted to ZnO by roasting (heating in excess air)
2ZnS + 3O2 → 2ZnO + 2SO2
common_errors: Confusion between roasting and calcination
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some answered correctly while others confused roasting with calcination.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct word from the brackets: __________ conducts electricity by the movement of ions. [Molten iron / Molten sodium chloride]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: molten sodium chloride / fused NaCl / Sodium chloride / NaCl / aqueous NaCl
key_points: Ionic compounds conduct electricity by movement of ions
Metals conduct electricity by movement of electrons, not ions
common_errors: Choosing molten iron due to lack of clarity about ionic vs metallic conduction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered molten iron instead of molten sodium chloride due to lack of clarity about ionic conduction.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct word from the brackets: The reaction that takes place at the anode during the electrolysis of aqueous Sodium argentocyanide with silver electrodes is ___________. [Ag → Ag+ + e– / Ag+ + e– → Ag]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Ag → Ag+ + e– / Ag - e– → Ag+
key_points: Oxidation occurs at anode — silver loses electron to form Ag+ ion
common_errors: Writing the cathode reaction instead of anode reaction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote the incorrect answer reflecting uncertainty about anode reaction.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct word from the brackets: The salt formed when ZnO reacts with hot concentrated NaOH is __________. [sodium zincate / zinc hydroxide]
key_points: ZnO is amphoteric; reacts with NaOH to form sodium zincate: ZnO + 2NaOH → Na2ZnO2 + H2O
common_errors: Choosing zinc hydroxide instead of sodium zincate
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified sodium zincate. Some incorrectly chose zinc hydroxide.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Match Column A with Column B:
Column A: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3
Column B options: 1. Vanadium Pentoxide, 2. Nickel, 3. Iron, 4. Concentrated Sulphuric acid, 5. Platinum
key_points: Iron is the catalyst in Haber's process for ammonia synthesis
common_errors: Confusing iron with platinum or vanadium pentoxide
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many answered correctly for first three parts. Some confused platinum with nickel.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Match Column A with Column B:
Column A: 4NH3 + 5O2 → 4NO + 6H2O
Column B options: 1. Vanadium Pentoxide, 2. Nickel, 3. Iron, 4. Concentrated Sulphuric acid, 5. Platinum
key_points: Platinum is the catalyst in catalytic oxidation of ammonia in Ostwald's process
common_errors: Confusing platinum with nickel
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates got confused differentiating platinum from nickel.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Match Column A with Column B:
Column A: 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3
Column B options: 1. Vanadium Pentoxide, 2. Nickel, 3. Iron, 4. Concentrated Sulphuric acid, 5. Platinum
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Column A (c) → Column B 1/5 (Vanadium Pentoxide / Platinum)
key_points: Vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) is the catalyst in Contact process for H2SO4 manufacture
Platinum can also be used
common_errors: Confusing concentrated sulphuric acid with vanadium pentoxide
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified vanadium pentoxide. Some confused concentrated H2SO4 with other options.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Match Column A with Column B:
Column A: C2H4 + H2 → C2H6
Column B options: 1. Vanadium Pentoxide, 2. Nickel, 3. Iron, 4. Concentrated Sulphuric acid, 5. Platinum
key_points: Nickel (or Platinum) is catalyst for hydrogenation of alkenes
common_errors: Confusing platinum from nickel
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates got confused differentiating platinum from nickel.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Match Column A with Column B:
Column A: CuSO4.5H2O → CuSO4 + 5H2O
Column B options: 1. Vanadium Pentoxide, 2. Nickel, 3. Iron, 4. Concentrated Sulphuric acid, 5. Platinum
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Column A (e) → Column B 4 (Concentrated Sulphuric acid)
key_points: Concentrated sulphuric acid is a dehydrating agent that removes water of crystallisation from CuSO4.5H2O
common_errors: Confusing concentrated sulphuric acid with other options
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates confused concentrated H2SO4 with other options.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structural diagram for the following organic compound: 2-methyl propene
marking_schemes.correct_answer: CH2=C(CH3)-CH3 structural formula showing double bond between C1 and C2 with methyl branch on C2
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Structural formula showing: H2C=C(CH3)-CH3 or equivalent correct structure with double bond and methyl group on C2
key_points: 4 carbon chain with double bond
Methyl branch on C2 carbon
Double bond between C1 and C2
Correct hydrogen count on each carbon
marking_schemes.model_answer: CH2=C(CH3)-CH3 with full structural formula showing all H atoms
common_errors: Drawing condensed formula instead of structural formula
Misplacing methyl group
Incorrectly counting hydrogen atoms
Adding extra hydrogen to carbon with double bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many could draw the structure. Some drew condensed formula. Some misplaced methyl group or incorrectly counted H atoms.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the structural diagram for the following organic compound: butanal
marking_schemes.correct_answer: CH3-CH2-CH2-CHO with full structural formula showing –CHO functional group with double bond to O
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Structural formula showing CH3-CH2-CH2-CHO with double bond oxygen on terminal carbon
key_points: 4 carbon chain
–CHO aldehyde group at terminal carbon (C1)
Double bond between C and O in CHO group shown
Correct tetravalency of all carbons
marking_schemes.model_answer: CH3-CH2-CH2-CHO (full structural formula with all bonds shown)
common_errors: Confusing –CHO with –OH or –COOH
Drawing condensed form instead of structural formula
Failing to show tetravalency of carbon
Incorrectly placing CHO group within the chain
Failing to show double bond of oxygen in butanal
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many drew the correct structural formula. Others confused –CHO with –OH or –COOH. Some drew condensed form.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give IUPAC name for the following organic compound: [Structure showing two carbons each with 2 Cl atoms — Cl2CH-CHCl2]
key_points: Ethane backbone (2 carbons)
4 chlorine atoms: 2 on C1 and 2 on C2
Prefix 'tetra' for 4 chlorine atoms
Correct numbering 1,1,2,2
common_errors: Not mentioning prefix 'tetra'
Using 'quadra' or 'quadri' instead of 'tetra'
Incorrect numbering of chlorine atoms
Omitting numbering entirely
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many correctly wrote 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane. Some omitted 'tetra' or used wrong prefixes. Some gave incorrect numbering.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give IUPAC name for the following organic compound: [Structure showing CH3-CH2-CH2-COOH — butanoic acid]
key_points: 4 carbon chain
Carboxylic acid functional group –COOH
Name: butanoic acid
common_errors: Writing butanol instead of butanoic acid
Omitting the word acid
Spelling errors
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified butanoic acid. Some wrote butanol or omitted 'acid'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give IUPAC name for the following organic compound: [Structure showing CH3-CH=CH-CH2-CH3 — pent-2-ene]
key_points: 5 carbon chain (pentene)
Double bond between C2 and C3
Lowest locant rule gives C2 for double bond
common_errors: Writing pentane instead of pent-2-ene
Incorrectly identifying longest carbon chain
Writing 1-methylbut-1-ene
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many confused IUPAC naming and wrote pentane. Common error was incorrectly identifying longest carbon chain.

marking_schemes.question_text: The atomic number of two atoms 'X' and 'Y' are 14 and 8 respectively. State the period to which 'X' belongs. (Do not identify X and Y)
key_points: X has atomic number 14: electronic configuration 2,8,4
3 shells occupied → Period 3
common_errors: Writing period number in Roman numeral (III) instead of Arabic numeral (3)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified Period 3. A few wrote Roman numeral III instead of Arabic numeral 3, losing marks.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: The atomic number of two atoms 'X' and 'Y' are 14 and 8 respectively. State the formula of the compound formed between 'X' and 'Y'. (Do not identify X and Y)
key_points: X (at. no. 14) has valency 4; Y (at. no. 8) has valency 2
Formula: XY2 (silicon dioxide equivalent)
common_errors: Providing name of compound instead of formula
Writing X2Y or X6Y12
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly wrote XY2. Some gave compound name. A few wrote X2Y or X6Y12.

marking_schemes.question_text: Justify the following statement: Anode is known as the oxidizing electrode.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Anions migrate to the anode and give up/lose electrons (and get oxidised) / Anode receives/gains electrons (causing oxidation) / Oxidation takes place at anode
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Anions or ions migrate to the anode and give up / lose electrons / donate electrons (and get oxidised) / Anode receives / gains electrons (causing oxidation) / Oxidation takes place
key_points: Anions migrate to anode and lose electrons
Oxidation occurs at anode (OIL — Oxidation Is Loss)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Anions migrate to the anode and lose electrons (get oxidised). Since oxidation occurs at the anode, it is called the oxidising electrode.

marking_schemes.question_text: An organic compound 'X' contains carbon, oxygen and hydrogen only. The percentage of carbon and hydrogen are 47.4% and 10.5% respectively. marking_schemes.scheme_text: C: 47.4%, O: 42.1%, H: 10.5%; Moles: C=47.4/12=3.95, O=42.1/16=2.63, H=10.5/1=10.5; Divide by smallest (2.63): C=1.5, O=1, H=4; Multiply by 2: C=3, O=2, H=8; Empirical formula = C3O2H8; n = 76/76 = 1; Molecular formula = C3O2H8
key_points: Number of moles: C=3.95, O=2.63, H=10.5
Divide by smallest (2.63): C=1.5, O=1, H=4
Multiply by 2 to get whole numbers: C=3, O=2, H=8
Empirical formula = C3O2H8
Empirical formula weight = 36+32+8 = 76
n = molecular mass / empirical formula mass = 76/76 = 1
Molecular formula = C3O2H8
marking_schemes.model_answer:
% O = 100 - 47.4 - 10.5 = 42.1%
Moles: C = 47.4/12 = 3.95; O = 42.1/16 = 2.63; H = 10.5/1 = 10.5
Divide by smallest (2.63): C = 1.5, O = 1, H = 4
Multiply by 2: C = 3, O = 2, H = 8
Empirical formula = C3O2H8
Empirical formula weight = 76
n = 76/76 = 1
Molecular formula = C3O2H8
common_errors: Determining empirical formula but failing to calculate molecular formula
Dividing atomic weights by percentage values (incorrect)
Not dividing moles by smallest number
Not multiplying empirical formula by n
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many determined empirical formula but failed to calculate molecular formula. Some divided atomic weights by percentages incorrectly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Acidulated water is electrolysed using platinum electrodes. What is the observation at the anode?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Bubbles of colourless gas released / Volume of gas collected is almost half of that collected at cathode / gas released rekindles glowing splinter / gas released turns alkaline pyrogallol solution brown
marking_schemes.scheme_text: bubbles of colourless gas released / Volume of gas collected is almost half of that collected at cathode / gas released rekindles glowing splinter / gas released turns alkaline pyrogallol solution brown
key_points: Oxygen gas is produced at anode
Volume of O2 = half volume of H2 produced at cathode
O2 rekindles a glowing splinter
marking_schemes.model_answer: Bubbles of colourless gas (oxygen) are released at the anode. The volume of gas is about half that collected at the cathode. The gas rekindles a glowing splinter.
common_errors: Only writing O2 is evolved without mentioning confirmatory test
Not stating that volume is half of hydrogen
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Oxygen was correctly identified. Some only wrote O2 is evolved without confirmatory test.

marking_schemes.question_text: State Avogadro's Law.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Under the same conditions of temperature and pressure, equal volumes of all gases contain the same number of molecules/particles.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Avogadro's Law: Under the same conditions of temperature and pressure equal volume of all gases contain the same number of molecules / particles.
key_points: Equal volumes
Same temperature and pressure
Same number of molecules
marking_schemes.model_answer: Under the same conditions of temperature and pressure, equal volumes of all gases contain the same number of molecules.
common_errors: Missing key phrase 'under the same temperature and pressure'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most stated correctly. A few missed key phrase 'under the same temperature and pressure'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Define Co-ordinate bond.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: The bond formed between two atoms by sharing a pair of electrons provided entirely by one of the combining atoms.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Co-ordinate bond: The bond formed between two atoms by sharing a pair of electrons provided entirely by one of the combining atoms.
key_points: Both electrons come from only one atom (donor)
The other atom is the acceptor
marking_schemes.model_answer: A coordinate bond (dative bond) is the bond formed between two atoms by sharing a pair of electrons provided entirely by one of the combining atoms.
common_errors: Confusing lone pairs with shared pairs of electrons in definition
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many could not define correctly and confused lone pairs with shared pairs.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Ammonium chloride and Sodium chloride using an alkali.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: NH4Cl reacts with alkali to produce pungent colourless ammonia gas which turns moist red litmus paper blue / dense white fumes with conc. HCl. NaCl shows no reaction / no gas evolved / no visible change.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: NH4Cl reacts with alkali to produce pungent colourless gas / or a gas which turns moist red litmus paper blue / any test for NH3 …. Dense white fumes with conc. HCl / turns Nessler's reagent brown; With NaCl - no reaction / no gas evolved / no visible change or reaction / no such observation
key_points: NH4Cl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O + NH3↑
NH3 identified by pungent smell, turning moist red litmus blue, white fumes with HCl
NaCl shows no reaction with alkali
marking_schemes.model_answer: NH4Cl reacts with alkali (NaOH) to produce pungent ammonia gas which turns moist red litmus paper blue. NaCl does not react with alkali — no gas evolved.
accepted_alternatives: dense white fumes with conc. HCl
common_errors: Writing reactions for both without specifying difference
Only saying colourless gas without identifying ammonia or confirmatory test
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many failed. Either wrote reactions for both or missed key confirmatory tests for ammonia. Common error: saying colourless gas without test.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Zinc Nitrate solution and Calcium Nitrate solution using excess sodium hydroxide solution.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Zinc nitrate gives a white gelatinous precipitate which dissolves in excess NaOH. Calcium nitrate gives a white precipitate which is insoluble in excess NaOH.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Zinc nitrate gives a (gelatinous)(white) precipitate which is soluble in excess of NaOH / ppt dissolves in excess of NaOH / clear solution formed. Calcium nitrate gives a (white) ppt which is insoluble in excess of NaOH / ppt does not dissolve in excess of NaOH / white ppt remains / sparingly soluble
key_points: Zn(NO3)2 + 2NaOH → Zn(OH)2 + 2NaNO3; Zn(OH)2 + 2NaOH(excess) → Na2ZnO2 + 2H2O (dissolves)
Ca(NO3)2 + 2NaOH → Ca(OH)2↓ + 2NaNO3; Ca(OH)2 insoluble in excess NaOH
marking_schemes.model_answer: Zinc nitrate: forms white gelatinous precipitate [Zn(OH)2] which dissolves in excess NaOH forming colourless solution. Calcium nitrate: forms white precipitate [Ca(OH)2] which remains insoluble in excess NaOH.
common_errors: Writing both as soluble or both as insoluble
Writing reaction for only one salt
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many couldn't differentiate. Several wrote either 'both soluble' or 'both insoluble'. Some wrote reaction for only one salt.

marking_schemes.question_text: From the compounds given (PbO, CH4, PbO2, CO2, HCl, NCl3, SO2), choose the compound which fits the description: A colourless gas which turns acidified K2Cr2O7 from orange to green.
key_points: SO2 is a reducing agent — reduces K2Cr2O7 from orange (Cr6+) to green (Cr3+)
CO2 does not affect acidified K2Cr2O7
common_errors: Choosing CO2 or CH4 instead of SO2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many chose SO2 correctly. A few incorrectly chose CO2 or CH4.

marking_schemes.question_text: From the compounds given (PbO, CH4, PbO2, CO2, HCl, NCl3, SO2), choose the compound which fits the description: A yellow explosive oily liquid formed when excess chlorine gas reacts with ammonia gas.
key_points: Excess Cl2 reacts with NH3 to form NCl3 (yellow, explosive, oily liquid)
NH3 + 3Cl2(excess) → NCl3 + 3HCl
common_errors: Missing the word 'excess' in question leading to wrong answer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many correctly identified NCl3. Others failed because they missed the word 'excess' in question.

marking_schemes.question_text: From the compounds given (PbO, CH4, PbO2, CO2, HCl, NCl3, SO2), choose the compound which fits the description: A yellow metallic oxide formed on thermal decomposition of PbCO3.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: PbO / Lead oxide / lead monoxide / Litharge
key_points: PbCO3 → PbO + CO2 (thermal decomposition)
PbO is yellow (litharge)
common_errors: Writing PbO2 or ZnO instead of PbO
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most correctly identified PbO. Some wrote PbO2 or ZnO.

marking_schemes.question_text: P = Simple displacement, Q = Neutralisation by titration, R = Precipitation, S = Direct combination. Choose the most appropriate method to prepare PbCl2.
key_points: PbCl2 is insoluble — best prepared by precipitation (double displacement)
e.g. Pb(NO3)2 + 2NaCl → PbCl2↓ + 2NaNO3
common_errors: Choosing method P (simple displacement) instead of R (precipitation)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many incorrectly chose method P instead of R. Some randomly chose a method.

marking_schemes.question_text: P = Simple displacement, Q = Neutralisation by titration, R = Precipitation, S = Direct combination. Choose the most appropriate method to prepare FeCl3.
key_points: FeCl3 is best prepared by direct combination of iron and chlorine: 2Fe + 3Cl2 → 2FeCl3
common_errors: Selecting incorrect method for ferric chloride preparation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. Some lost marks for selecting incorrect method.

marking_schemes.question_text: P = Simple displacement, Q = Neutralisation by titration, R = Precipitation, S = Direct combination. Choose the most appropriate method to prepare Na2SO4.
key_points: Na2SO4 is soluble — prepared by neutralisation of NaOH with H2SO4 by titration
2NaOH + H2SO4 → Na2SO4 + 2H2O
common_errors: Confusing with simple displacement
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most identified neutralisation by titration. A few confused with simple displacement.
